headline: Recommended $500,000 for city retirements, $100,000 for a Traveling Tooth Fairy dental program, and a $35,000 transfer to the Nashua Association for the Elderly.
summary: Members considered resolution R-26-048, a $1,607,694.55 supplemental appropriation, and voted on each item separately. They recommended funding for Ledge Street playground equipment, city retirements, a dental program, and park and field rehabilitation, and voted 6-1 for final passage of R-26-048. They also recommended final passage of R-26-050 and O-26-017.
decisions: Approved motion to vote on each item in R-26-048 separately, 7-0.
Rescinded Johnson's motion to remove the Ledge Street playground equipment and Traveling Tooth Fairy dental program lines from R-26-048.
Recommended approval of funding from Miscellaneous Revenue Account #45999 for Ledge Street playground equipment, 7-0.
Recommended $100,000 for the dental program for the Traveling Tooth Fairy, 7-0.
Recommended $500,000 for funding upcoming city retirements, 6-1, with Johnson opposed.
Approved $40,000 for lead grant activity salaries and non-salary expenses, 5-2, with Sennott and Johnson opposed.
Recommended $5,250.00 from the Park Rehabilitation Expendable Trust Fund for parking field rehabilitation, funded from facility rental fees, 7-0.
Recommended $42,758.50 from the Park Rehabilitation Expendable Trust Fund for park and field rehabilitation, funded out of field rental fees, 7-0.
Recommended $672,299.87 for the FEMA Public Assistance grant activity to cover COVID-19 salaries and wage expenses, 6-1, with Johnson opposed.
Approved final passage of R-26-048, 6-1, with Johnson opposed.
Recommended final passage of R-26-050, which transfers $35,000 for the Nashua Association for the Elderly, 7-0.
Recommended final passage of O-26-017, which removes the language for a Solid Waste Equipment Reserve Fund and discontinues the fund, 7-0.
